badges.outline: A printable US Letter portrait page (8.5 by 11 inches) for a kids' pretend-play game, drawn flat and straight-on and filling the whole image: the page itself, not a photo or mockup of paper. Plain white paper with a clean white margin of about half an inch on every side where nothing is drawn, so it prints on a home printer. The game is "Moon Bakery" (a bakery on the moon). Art style for the whole kit: coloring-page version of a friendly flat vector cartoon: black outlines only on white paper, thick clean even lines, soft rounded shapes, no color, no gray, no shading, no filled black areas, every shape open for a 5-year-old to color in. Letters are bold outlined bubble letters that can be colored in too. Draw a sheet of exactly 6 lanyard name badges in a strict grid of 3 columns and 2 rows, filling the page: every piece exactly the same size and shape, evenly spaced, with equal wide plain white gutters between them and nothing at all drawn in the gutters, each piece whole inside its own cell, never touching or overlapping another piece. Each one: tall rounded-rectangle tags with a punched hole and a little clip at the top center, a themed decorative border, one character picture in the upper half, the role title under it on a ribbon banner, and at the bottom the word "Name:" followed by a long blank line to write on. In order, left to right, top to bottom: badge 1: a cute cartoon character as the head baker (bakes the moon bread), title "Head Baker"; badge 2: a cute cartoon character as the cupcake chef (frosts the cupcakes), title "Cupcake Chef"; badge 3: a cute cartoon character as the delivery rover (drives treats to the craters), title "Delivery Rover"; badge 4: a cute cartoon character as the customer (orders yummy treats), title "Customer"; badge 5: a cute cartoon character as the cashier (takes the moon coins), title "Cashier"; badge 6: a cute cartoon character as the taste tester (tries every treat), title "Taste Tester". The ONLY words on the page, spelled exactly letter for letter: "Head Baker", "Cupcake Chef", "Delivery Rover", "Customer", "Cashier", "Taste Tester", "Name:". "Name:" appears once on every badge (6 times). Big, clear, rounded print letters, easy for a 5-year-old to read, dark on a light background, never curved along a path, never tiny. No other words, letters, numbers or signatures anywhere. Every badge identical in shape and size so they look like a set. Thin gray dashed cut lines around each piece, with wide white gutters between pieces so scissors fit. Kid-friendly and gentle, for ages 4 to 8: no guns, no knives, no swords, no weapons of any kind (not even toy ones), no blood, nothing scary, violent or grown-up, no real people, no brands, no text other than the words given. No skulls, no crossbones, no skeletons: pirates and their flags are friendly and cheerful. Pirate ships have no cannons; knights hold shields, never swords.
